Q218452.label: 26th of July Movement
Q218452.summary: The 26 July Movement, initially simply "The Movement", was a Cuban vanguard revolutionary organization and later a political party led by Fidel Castro. The movement's name commemorates the failed 1953 attack on the Moncada Barracks in Santiago de Cuba, part of an attempt to overthrow the dictator Fulgencio Batista. M-26-7 is considered the leading organization of the Cuban Revolution.

Q17072980.label: 1957 Honduran Constituent Assembly election
Q17072980.summary: Constituent Assembly elections were held in Honduras on 22 September 1957. In November the Assembly elected Ramón Villeda Morales as president.

Q125627220.label: 2026 Hungarian parliamentary election
Q125627220.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Hungary on 12 April 2026 to elect all 199 members of the National Assembly. It was the 10th parliamentary election and the highest-turnout election since Hungary's transition to democracy in 1990.

Q54982996.label: Mamuka Bakhtadze
Q54982996.summary: Mamuka Bakhtadze is a Georgian politician who served as the country's prime minister from 20 June 2018 until 2 September 2019. Bakhtadze announced his official statement about resignation via Facebook post. He had previously served as minister of finance (2017–2018) and, prior to that, executive director of the Georgian Railway company (2013–2017).

Q1627476.label: 1936 Norwegian parliamentary election
Q1627476.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Norway on 19 October 1936, the last before World War II and the German invasion of Norway. The result was a victory for the Labour Party, which won 70 of the 150 seats in the Storting.

Q28062036.label: Turkish constitutional referendum, 2017
Q28062036.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Turkey on 16 April 2017 on whether to approve 18 proposed amendments to the Turkish constitution that were brought forward by the governing Justice and Development Party (AKP) and the Nationalist Movement Party (MHP).

Q335188.label: Saitō Makoto
Q335188.summary: Viscount Saitō Makoto was a Japanese admiral and politician who was prime minister of Japan from 1932 to 1934. Upon distinguishing himself during his command of two cruisers in the First Sino-Japanese War, Saitō rose rapidly to the rank of rear admiral by 1900. He was promoted to vice admiral during the Russo-Japanese War in 1904. After serving as Minister of the Navy from 1906 to 1914, Saitō held the position of Governor-General of Korea from 1919 to 1927 and again from 1929 to 1931.

Q2237268.label: Battle of Umm Qasr
Q2237268.desc: 2003 first military confrontation in the Iraq War
Q2237268.summary: The Battle of Umm Qasr was the first military confrontation in the Iraq War. At the start of the war, one of the first objectives was the port of Umm Qasr. On 21 March 2003, as allied forces advanced across Southern Iraq, an amphibious landing force captured the new port area of Umm Qasr.

Q1713492.label: Young Czech Party
Q1713492.summary: The Young Czechs, officially National Liberal Party (Czech: Národní strana svobodomyslná) was formed in the Bohemian crown land of Austria-Hungary in 1874. It initiated the democratization of Czech political parties and led to the establishment of the political base of Czechoslovakia.
